summary: The endpoint itself (app/api/health/route.ts) is Next.js application code, not infrastructure — that belongs to a backend/app engineer. My role is to define how 'version' and 'environment' are sourced at runtime without new secrets or services, confirm there is no CI/CD or Docker surface to wire up, and flag deployment/observability concerns (no leaking build metadata, no new env vars needed). No Dockerfile, vercel.json, or .github/workflows exist in this repo (only inside node_modules) — deployment is handled by Vercel's zero-config Next.js build, so there is no pipeline file to edit for this feature.
areas_affected: deployment config (none exists — Vercel auto-detects Next.js, nothing to add)
docs:check script compliance for new API.md

proposed_tasks.description: Specify the exact runtime sourcing for 'version' and 'environment' fields so the app engineer doesn't invent ad-hoc env vars: version = package.json 'version' field (currently 0.1.0) imported at build time (no new env var needed, no secret exposure); environment = Vercel's auto-injected VERCEL_ENV ('production' | 'preview' | 'development'), falling back to NODE_ENV when running outside Vercel (local dev). No new environment variables need to be created or added to Vercel project settings.

Confirm no Docker/CI/CD changes are required: repo has no Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, vercel.json, or .github/workflows at the project root (Vercel builds via its default Next.js detection). Document this as a non-task so the feature isn't blocked waiting on infra config that doesn't exist.

(Optional, out of scope unless requested) Propose a lightweight post-deploy smoke check hitting /api/health once it exists, as a future CI/CD addition — flagged as a stretch goal, not required by the feature request.

DEPENDENCY (not my ownership): implement app/api/health/route.ts using NextResponse, returning { status, version, environment } per the sourcing defined in infra-1. This is application/business logic under app/, owned by a backend/app engineer, not infrastructure.

DEPENDENCY (not my ownership): add Vitest test(s) for the route handler (e.g. tests/api/health.test.ts), following the existing vi.stubEnv() pattern seen in data-fallback.test.ts to assert correct environment reporting under different VERCEL_ENV/NODE_ENV values.

DEPENDENCY (not my ownership): add brief API documentation (e.g. docs/engineering/API.md or a section in PROJECT_GUIDE.md) describing the endpoint contract, and register it in docs/index/MASTER_INDEX.md so npm run docs:check does not fail.

contracts: version field value MUST come from package.json's 'version' field (currently '0.1.0') — no new build-time env var or git-sha plumbing needed.
environment field value MUST be sourced from process.env.VERCEL_ENV with fallback to process.env.NODE_ENV — do not introduce a custom env var for this.
No new environment variables need to be added to Vercel project settings for this feature.
risks: If the app engineer adds a new custom env var (e.g. APP_VERSION, APP_ENV) instead of reusing VERCEL_ENV/package.json version, it creates unnecessary secrets-wiring overhead in Vercel project settings across dev/preview/prod with no added value.
The health response must not leak sensitive build/runtime details (internal hostnames, full env var dumps, stack traces) — restrict to status/version/environment only.

Since there is no existing app/api/ directory, this is the first REST route in the app — Turbopack/Next.js 16 route handler conventions should be double-checked against node_modules/next/dist/docs/ per AGENTS.md before implementation, as this project explicitly warns that API conventions may differ from training data.
tests: Automated test ownership belongs to the app/backend engineer, not infra — no infrastructure-level tests (e.g. pipeline tests, container tests) are needed since there is no Docker/CI surface in this repo.
questions_or_unknowns: Should the environment value be the raw VERCEL_ENV string ('production'/'preview'/'development') or mapped to a project-specific label? No existing convention in the codebase for this — needs a decision from whoever owns app-1.

Is a post-deploy smoke check (infra-3) actually wanted, or is this feature scoped to the endpoint + tests + docs only, as the request states? Recommend treating infra-3 as explicitly out of scope unless the user confirms otherwise.
